# Data

Describe the data source, inclusion criteria and exclusions. The example file,
`data/example-trial.csv`, is the `trial` dataset from the gtsummary package: simulated data
for 200 patients on two drugs. Replace it with your own files.

```{r data}
# List every file the report reads, so the checksum table below covers all of them.
workDir="D:\\OneDrive - VUMC\\work\\EvanBrittain\\"
dataFile=""

input_files <- c(trial = "data/example-trial.csv")
dat <- utils::read.csv(input_files[["trial"]])
```

Each input file's MD5 checksum is a fingerprint of its exact contents: if the file changes in
any way, the checksum changes. It shows which version of the data produced this report.

```{r input-files}
print(data.frame(file = unname(input_files), bytes = file.size(input_files),
                 md5 = unname(tools::md5sum(input_files))), row.names = FALSE)
```

# Results

Tables and figures are numbered automatically. Refer to them by label, as in the sentences
below, so the numbers stay right when you add, remove or move one.

## Baseline characteristics

@tbl-baseline shows baseline characteristics by treatment. Continuous variables: mean (SD);
categorical variables: n (%).

::: {.report-table .table-standard}
```{r}
#| label: tbl-baseline
#| tbl-cap: "Baseline characteristics by treatment."
dat |>
  gtsummary::tbl_summary(
    by = trt, include = c(age, marker, stage, grade),
    label = list(age ~ "Age (years)", marker ~ "Marker level (ng/mL)",
                 stage ~ "T stage", grade ~ "Grade"),
    statistic = list(gtsummary::all_continuous() ~ "{mean} ({sd})",
                     gtsummary::all_categorical() ~ "{n} ({p}%)"),
    digits = gtsummary::all_continuous() ~ 1,
    missing = "ifany", missing_text = "Missing"
  ) |>
  gtsummary::add_overall(last = FALSE) |>
  gtsummary::bold_labels() |>
  gtsummary::as_gt() |>
  style_gt()
```
:::

## Small table

A static summary table for the report text. @tbl-marker-grade gives the marker level by
treatment and tumour grade.

::: {.report-table .table-standard}
```{r}
#| label: tbl-marker-grade
#| tbl-cap: "Marker level (ng/mL) by treatment and grade."
dat |>
  dplyr::filter(!is.na(marker)) |>
  dplyr::group_by(trt, grade) |>
  dplyr::summarise(n = dplyr::n(), mean = mean(marker), sd = sd(marker), .groups = "drop") |>
  gt::gt(groupname_col = "trt") |>
  gt::cols_label(grade = "Grade", n = "N", mean = "Mean", sd = "SD") |>
  gt::fmt_number(columns = c(mean, sd), decimals = 2) |>
  gt::tab_source_note("Patients with a missing marker level are excluded.") |>
  style_gt()
```
:::

## Downloadable table

All rows are stored in this HTML file. Readers can search, sort and download them.

::: {.report-table .table-standard}
```{r results-table}
result_table(dat, "trial-data")
```
:::

## Figure

@fig-marker shows marker level against age for each treatment.

::: {.figure-standard}
```{r}
#| label: fig-marker
#| fig-cap: "Marker level by age and treatment."
ggplot(dat, aes(age, marker, colour = trt, shape = trt)) +
  geom_point(size = 2.5, alpha = 0.8) +
  scale_colour_manual(values = report_palette) +
  labs(x = "Age (years)", y = "Marker level (ng/mL)", colour = NULL, shape = NULL)
```
:::
